Subject: Performance SLO & Context Window follow-up (FinCo)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the actions we discussed so your team has a single place to refer to.

Summary of FinCo requirements (from call):
- Target latency: p95 <= 400ms for interactive completions (streaming enabled).
- Throughput/scale: baseline 200 concurrent active users; peak bursts to ~600 concurrent requests.
- Typical input size: 400–800 input tokens (prompts + history).
- Typical output size: 150–800 tokens; a subset of flows require up to ~2k output tokens (batch-style reports).
- Streaming: required for interactive chat (token-by-token streaming). Also need reliable finalization for long outputs.
- Concurrency & throughput SLOs: 95th percentile under sustained load of 250 rps with 600 concurrent sessions.

Notes on context window impact (high level):
- Larger context windows (1k–8k tokens) increase per-request memory and KV cache pressure; cold-start generation times can be higher.
- For streaming, total time-to-first-token is dominated by model startup and batching policy; subsequent token latency depends on batching and kernel perf.
- When outputs approach 1k+ tokens, end-to-end completion time grows linearly with output tokens; chunked streaming mitigates perceived latency but increases total processing.

Recommended next steps (agreed):
1) We will run a perf baseline using a representative prompt set you provide (please send sample prompts + any auth'd test account).
2) Redwood will propose a config (model size, quantization, batching params, Dedicated vs Hosted) with cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) We’ll schedule a technical perf hook (30–60m) with your infra/eng team to align on load shape and networking.

I attached our perf snapshot deck with examples of p50/p95 under different context windows and streaming configs — this should give rough expectations while we run your workload.

Attachments: redwood-performance-metrics.pdf (high-level), please send finco-prompt-set-sample.csv when ready.

Action items for FinCo:
- Samir / Priya: share sample prompt set + a single test API key or staging endpoint (or let us use a transient workload against your infra).
- Confirm whether the 2k-output flows need strict end-to-end SLOs or can be batch-processed with relaxed latency (e.g., 30s SLA).
- Please confirm preferred time window for the perf run (your timezone).

I’ll follow up with proposed configuration options and a calendar invite for the perf hook.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — super helpful. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with the platform team:

Load shape & SLAs:
- Baseline: 200 concurrent active users translating to ~180 rps.
- Peak: ~600 concurrent -> short spikes up to 650 rps (5–10 min bursts).
- We care most about p95 latency for interactive chat flows (where users expect near-instant replies). For these flows we want p95 <= 400ms for responses up to 512 tokens.
- For long-report flows (1k–2k output tokens), we’re okay with a higher p95 (<= 8s) if we can stream partial results to the UI as they generate.

Context window specifics:
- Average prompt + history: ~620 tokens.
- 80% of messages will have output <= 300 tokens; 15% 300–800 tokens; 5% > 1k tokens.
- We will provide a 200-row sample prompt set and 20 long-report examples.

Networking & infra constraints:
- All traffic routes via our VPC peering (low-latency cross-AZ).
- Our infra team prefers Dedicated capacity for predictable tail latency; open to Redwood Hosted for PoC.

Questions:
1) For the interactive flow, can Redwood guarantee p95 <= 400ms at the scale above with streaming enabled for an 8k context window, or would you recommend a smaller model + KV cache + quantization?
2) Any recommendations on max tokens we should enforce client-side to avoid service degradation?

We’ll upload the prompt set to the Drive link you shared by tomorrow.

- Samir

Samir —

Great questions. Short answers up front, followed by recommended config and next steps.

Q1 — p95 <= 400ms at 8k context: not with a single large model instance under your peak shape unless we use aggressive sharding + very high-spec Dedicated instances. In practice we recommend:
- For interactive chat with strict p95 <= 400ms for up to 512-token responses: use a smaller/optimized model variant (e.g., 13B quantized) with KV cache + streaming. That configuration hit p95 ~250–350ms in our internal perf runs at similar concurrency when placed on Dedicated pools and with conservative batching.
- For 8k context windows + long outputs (1k–2k), we recommend separating the flows: keep interactive chat on an optimized smaller model (pin to 13B q4/INT8) and route long-report generation to a larger model (70B or 100B) with relaxed latency SLOs (<= 8s) and streaming. This preserves UX while controlling cost.

Q2 — client-side max tokens: recommend soft caps + warnings:
- Soft cap on input context to 4k tokens for interactive routing (drop/trim oldest history beyond that).
- Hard cap: 8k tokens unless you provision Dedicated with larger memory footprints.
- Output caps: 1k tokens for interactive flows; allow up to 2k for batch/report endpoints.

Recommended config (initial PoC):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated (predictable tail latency).
- Model routing: interactive -> 13B q4 with streaming; report -> 70B float/quantized with KV cache.
- Capacity: start with 4 Dedicated serving nodes of A100-class (or equivalent), autoscale policy to add 2 nodes on sustained CPU/GPU busy > 70% for 10m.
- Batching: small batch windows for interactive (10–20ms), target batch size 4–8. Larger batches for report workloads.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated context patterns.

Next steps:
1) Please upload the sample prompt set + 20 long-report examples to the Drive link.
2) Neha — can you prepare an initial pricing estimate for Dedicated baseline + 2 burst nodes? (cc’ed)
3) Rafael — can your team run a quick perf trace with the suggested smaller model + streaming on our infra lab and share p50/p95 numbers? (cc’ed)
4) Samir / Priya — propose 30–60m time slots for a perf run next week.

I’ll attach a short checklist and a sample config JSON after this thread (so you can drop it into your infra tests).

Thanks —
Marissa
